audit: People, administration, content and personal workspaces UX source review
method: Read-only inspection of routes, page components, nested dialogs, helpers, store use, API services, owned backend controller actions and HR setup SQL/domain definitions. Report artifact only; no application edits, database calls, server startup or runtime UI verification.

backend_cross_check.area: HR salary and leave setup foundation
backend_cross_check.status: Database/domain foundation exists, but no matching maintenance API or frontend setup surface was found
backend_cross_check.details: LeaveType has AnnualQuota and IsPaidLeave. SQL defines salary structures, earning/deduction components, structure-component amounts and effective employee salary assignments. The HR controller actions, HrRequests and IHrService contain no CRUD/assignment commands for those setup records. Do not describe these as a ready hidden API. Payroll processing depends on those records and excludes employees with no matching salary setup.

backend_cross_check.status: Shift policy fields are exposed; generic rule/calendar maintenance API was not found
backend_cross_check.details: Shift start/end/grace/night/weekly hours are API-backed and present in the form. Holiday/WeekOff are attendance statuses; no holiday-calendar, configurable attendance rule or leave-entitlement maintenance controller action was found. Attendance adjustment request/decision APIs exist but no list/search endpoint for an adjustments approval inbox was found in AttendanceController.

backend_cross_check.status: Monthly report is integrated in a nested employee dialog; department report remains API/service-only in the inspected frontend
backend_cross_check.details: EmployeeAttendanceModal calls getMonthlyReport. DepartmentReport controller action, frontend service and Redux thunk exist, but no page/component caller or dispatch for the department-report thunk was found.

backend_cross_check.status: Exposed backend actions are represented in nested frontend surfaces
backend_cross_check.details: Reporting-manager/dropdown helpers, employee details/create/update/delete, resign/rejoin, documents list/add/delete and bank details list/add all have corresponding page/form/profile/service usage. These are not missing merely because there is no separate sidebar link.

backend_cross_check.status: Core master and child mapping endpoints have frontend surfaces
backend_cross_check.details: Users CRUD/export/activate/deactivate/role assignment, Roles CRUD/export, Pages CRUD with parent hierarchy and role permission get/save are represented. Self-profile get/update exists in AuthController despite the frontend compatibility fallback copy. Account profile and HR employee profile are distinct resources.

backend_cross_check.area: Website masters, content children and warranty workflow
backend_cross_check.status: Controller-supported admin content/workflow actions are represented
backend_cross_check.details: Products CRUD with embedded benefits/media; posts CRUD; categories list/create/update/delete in the Categories tab; announcements CRUD; settings get/update; dashboard overview; warranty list/detail/history/attachment download, assign/start review/request information/approve/reject/resolve/complete, notes/customer messages and summary all have frontend service and screen/action counterparts. Media upload is a supporting capability, not a master. No additional standalone website master was identified in these controllers.

coverage.classification: Operational overview, not a master
coverage.flow: HR overview -> review staff, attendance and leave workload -> related HR screen.
coverage.existing_strength: Clear named metrics and attendance trend.
coverage.opportunity: Make pending approval cards and department counts open filtered lists with context.

coverage.classification: Master
coverage.flow: Create department code/name/description/active state -> use in designations and employees.
coverage.existing_strength: Simple form, common controls, server field-error mapping and read-only view mode.
coverage.opportunity: One setup workspace showing each department's designations and staff would reduce menu switching.

coverage.classification: Master linked to department
coverage.flow: Choose/create department -> create designation -> assign to employee.
coverage.existing_strength: Department can already be created inline; this shortcut should be preserved.
coverage.opportunity: Surface designation creation inside a department setup/detail panel and keep the created parent selected.

coverage.classification: Master with embedded attendance settings
coverage.flow: Configure shift -> assign employee -> use attendance operations.
coverage.existing_strength: Relevant timing and grace settings are already together.
coverage.opportunity: Show a human-readable duration/overnight preview and explain weekly hours before saving.

coverage.classification: Employee master; addresses/bank/documents are embedded child records; resign/rejoin are lifecycle actions
coverage.flow: Department/designation/shift -> employee identity/contact/employment -> optional addresses/bank -> save -> profile -> documents/attendance/leaves -> resign or rejoin.
coverage.existing_strength: A useful unified employee profile already exists with bank, documents, attendance and leave tabs. Create drafts and inline related-master creation already exist.
coverage.opportunity: Use a short onboarding form followed by optional sections; make PDF download explicit and distinguish bank-save failure from employee-save success.

coverage.classification: Daily transactions and approval workflow, not a master
coverage.flow: Select date/department -> mark visible staff -> review exceptions -> save -> correct individual attendance -> request/approve adjustment.
coverage.existing_strength: The quick attendance book already matches the desired sheet-like daily workflow and supports save/reset.
coverage.opportunity: Protect unsaved edits on date/navigation changes and replace manual adjustment IDs with a pending corrections inbox.

coverage.classification: Application and approval workflow; leave types are fixed enum options in this frontend
coverage.flow: Choose employee/type/dates/reason -> apply -> manager reviews pending leave -> approve/reject/cancel -> review balance and history.
coverage.existing_strength: Employee and manager selectors use display options; row actions prefill leave IDs; current-page statistics explicitly state their scope.
coverage.opportunity: Show balances as named days remaining/used, retain context in approval dialogs and unify pending approvals with the list.

coverage.classification: Period processing and approval workflow, not a salary-component master
screens_and_children: Selected payroll run and employee rows
coverage.flow: Select payroll month/year -> process -> review totals and employee values -> approve selected run -> inspect employee history/payslip.
coverage.existing_strength: Process and approval are distinct steps; employee payslip queries already use an employee selector.
coverage.opportunity: A review/approve step with period and staff context, a formatted printable payslip, and labelled query controls would make payroll client-ready.

coverage.area: HR embedded policies and enum configuration
coverage.classification: Embedded shift settings and fixed frontend enum options; no separate maintenance route found
coverage.flow: Configured shift and fixed option sets feed employee, attendance and leave forms.
coverage.existing_strength: Consistent shared option definitions.
coverage.opportunity: Database/domain leave quotas and salary setup records exist, but corresponding maintenance controller/service commands and frontend screens were not found. Add an agreed setup API and client setup surface, plus payroll readiness checks; configurable holiday/rule maintenance was not found either.

coverage.classification: Access-account master, separate from employee master
coverage.flow: Create account -> assign selected role -> activate/deactivate or update -> inspect effective permissions through role administration.
coverage.existing_strength: Validation and role selection are explicit; destructive/status actions already have confirmations.
coverage.opportunity: Guide Create account -> Assign role -> Review access in one flow and recover cleanly from a failed second API call.

coverage.classification: Master
coverage.flow: Create role -> configure page/action permissions -> assign role to users.
coverage.existing_strength: Small, understandable role form and confirmation dialogs.
coverage.opportunity: After creation, open permissions for that role; offer reviewed role templates/copy as a future speed improvement.

coverage.classification: Role-to-page/action mapping, not a separate business master
coverage.flow: Select role -> change page/action permissions -> save -> use role on account.
coverage.existing_strength: Search, bulk toggles, dirty status and read-only SuperAdmin access already exist.
coverage.opportunity: Guard unsaved role changes; show an impact summary of added/removed actions before saving broad changes.

coverage.classification: Technical navigation/resource master with parent-child hierarchy
coverage.flow: Configure page resource/route -> choose parent/icon/order -> map permissions -> navigation consumes configured records.
coverage.existing_strength: Tree view, add-child shortcut and descendant-parent prevention are already implemented.
coverage.opportunity: Keep this technical setup in an administrator area and provide a navigation preview plus clearer route/resource-name explanations.

coverage.classification: Content/service operations overview, not a master
coverage.flow: Review content/service workload -> open warranty queue or claim.
coverage.existing_strength: Recent claims already drill down directly.
coverage.opportunity: Add task-oriented shortcuts for draft posts/products and unassigned claims if those queues are supported.

coverage.classification: Public content/catalogue master, distinct from inventory item master; benefits/media are child rows
coverage.flow: Create draft product -> enter public product values/benefits/media -> choose primary image -> review public status -> save -> public catalogue consumes values.
coverage.existing_strength: Grouped sections, media validation/upload busy state, primary image control, sticky Save, transition confirmation and row-version conflict resolution.
coverage.opportunity: A client-facing product-card/full-page preview and Basics-first progressive entry would simplify the long form.

coverage.classification: Nested content category master
coverage.flow: Create category -> select category when writing blog post.
coverage.existing_strength: Categories already exist in a nested tab; automatic slug and conflict handling exist.
coverage.opportunity: Offer an inline Add category shortcut from the post editor when authorized, using the existing category form.

coverage.classification: Content records with category relation
coverage.flow: Choose/create category -> write draft -> add media/SEO -> preview -> choose publishing state/time -> save.
coverage.existing_strength: Auto slug, grouped content/publishing/SEO, explicit publishing state and conflict resolution.
coverage.opportunity: Render a faithful website preview while preserving the stored plain/Markdown contract; current Preview displays source text.

coverage.classification: Scheduled public content configuration
coverage.flow: Compose top-bar message/CTA -> choose priority/time window -> activate -> public site displays eligible announcement.
coverage.existing_strength: Live status explains eligibility, scheduled windows and dismissal-version helper already exist.
coverage.opportunity: Show a visual top-bar preview, client local time with timezone label and a clear ordering explanation in the form.

coverage.classification: Service case workflow, not a master
coverage.flow: Customer submission -> staff queue -> inspect detail/evidence -> assign/review -> approve or reject -> resolve refund/replacement/repair -> record history and customer communication.
coverage.existing_strength: Permission/status-aware guarded actions, required rejection reason, separate internal/customer messages and confirmed sends.
coverage.opportunity: A status board or saved My open/unassigned views can complement the table; show only useful next actions and hide technical backend explanations from client-facing report UI.

coverage.classification: Server-provided key/value settings, no client-side key creation
coverage.flow: Load centrally defined keys -> edit value/visibility -> save settings set -> website consumes allowed values.
coverage.existing_strength: No invented setting keys; visibility warning and dirty indicators are explicit.
coverage.opportunity: Map approved keys to friendly labels, help text and typed controls; review visibility changes and protect unsaved refresh/navigation.

coverage.classification: Reusable public/private entries; sheet is a category string, not a separately persisted master; column aliases are local display preferences
coverage.flow: Choose/create sheet -> type or paste Excel block -> preview -> review dirty rows -> save -> find/copy values -> inspect history/conflicts.
coverage.existing_strength: A substantial sheet-like workflow already exists; preview protects bulk paste, row states show saved/failed, private scope and conflicts are handled.
coverage.opportunity: Protect dirty sheet/view/navigation changes and offer recoverable local drafts; clarify browser-local column aliases and sheet persistence after first row.

coverage.classification: Signed-in account profile, separate from employee master
coverage.flow: Review own account -> edit name/email if supported -> save; use dedicated password flow.
coverage.existing_strength: Small account form, field conflict handling and explicit read-only fallback.
coverage.opportunity: Use client language for service-unavailable fallback and clarify account profile versus employee profile.

coverage.classification: Browser-local appearance/table/invoice/item preferences, not database or company configuration
coverage.flow: Choose appearance/template/table preference -> save immediately in this browser -> affected UI reads local preference.
coverage.existing_strength: Live appearance changes and visual invoice template choices.
coverage.opportunity: Group personal display preferences coherently and label persistence/scope; distinguish local manufacturing visibility from company/backend setup.

coverage.classification: Audit evidence, not a master or daily data-entry screen
screens_and_children: Filtered CSV export with cap notice
coverage.flow: Filter activity -> open event -> inspect actor/changes/before-after -> export or share support reference.
coverage.existing_strength: Readable changed-field comparison is primary; raw JSON and technical filters are already in disclosures. Export limit is clearly disclosed.
coverage.opportunity: Use this disclosure/diff pattern as a model for other screens and add related business-record links where entity routing is known.

findings.title: Dirty daily work can be silently discarded by changing context
findings.observed: Attendance changeSelectedDate clears all drafts immediately. Data Book sheet selection changes state immediately and remounts a keyed grid; grid cleanup cancels autosave timers. Pasted rows intentionally stay dirty until saved. Permissions selecting another role resets the matrix and dirty state immediately. No unsaved-navigation guard was found in these owned page/component/hook sources.
findings.impact: An operator can mark attendance, paste rows or edit permissions and lose work by choosing another date/sheet/role before saving.
findings.recommendation: Use a consistent Save changes / Keep draft / Discard choice before context switches, refresh and navigation; keep recoverable drafts. Preserve explicit Save review for pasted bulk rows.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed reset/remount paths; browser reproduction remains unperformed.

findings.title: HR approvals and corrections expose internal IDs instead of business context
findings.observed: Attendance correction requires Attendance Record ID. Attendance approve/reject opens an empty Adjustment ID input. Leave action dialogs prefill but allow editing Leave Application ID and Employee ID. Payroll approval similarly exposes an editable Run ID.
findings.impact: Nontechnical staff must find technical identifiers and can approve/correct a record without seeing its employee/date/period context.
findings.recommendation: Open corrections from an attendance row, provide a pending-adjustments inbox, and show employee/date/current/proposed values in approval dialogs. Bind IDs internally. Leave approval should show type/dates/days/balance; payroll approval should show period/headcount/totals.
findings.verification: Directly observed in form controls and initial state. API-side validation/authorization was not tested.

findings.title: Core HR results remain raw JSON
findings.observed: The Leave Balance panel and Payroll Payslip panel use JSON.stringify in a pre element.
findings.impact: Client staff cannot quickly read entitlement/used/remaining days or issue a normal payslip.
findings.recommendation: Render leave balance cards/table by leave type and a formatted employee-period payslip with earnings, deductions, net amount and print/download. Keep raw payload only in an optional administrator disclosure if useful.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed output formatting; authenticated response fields still require verification.

findings.title: Multi-request saves can leave partly completed account or employee setup
findings.observed: User create/update is followed by a separate role-assignment request. Employee edit is followed by a separate bank-details save. A second-request failure enters a general save error path after the first operation has already succeeded.
findings.impact: The operator may retry account creation or assume no employee update occurred, causing duplicate attempts or an unnoticed missing role/bank change.
findings.recommendation: Prefer an atomic supported API operation. Otherwise retain the created ID, show exactly which step succeeded, refresh the saved entity and offer Retry role assignment / Retry bank update without recreating the record.
findings.verification: Conditional failure risk confirmed by request order; no failure was injected and no production defect is claimed.

findings.title: Employee onboarding has too much work in its first save
findings.observed: The create/edit page combines identity, contact, employment, addresses and bank data. After create it automatically generates a profile PDF before navigating.
findings.impact: Simple onboarding requires a long form and an unexpected PDF action. Optional data competes with required staff setup.
findings.recommendation: Keep essential identity/contact/employment first; use optional address/bank/document steps, a completion checklist and explicit Save / Save and download profile actions. Preserve existing create drafts and inline lookup creation.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed form grouping and automatic PDF call.

findings.title: Website content editors need a faithful public preview
findings.observed: Blog Preview displays content in a whitespace-preserving text div, so Markdown source remains text. Product form exposes public data in many sections without a public product preview. Announcements expose message/CTA/order/time values in a form without a top-bar preview.
findings.impact: Editors cannot confidently judge the customer-facing result before publishing.
findings.recommendation: Use shared website renderers or a safe preview page for posts/product cards/top bars, preserving current storage and API contracts. Show Draft -> Preview -> Publish as the client-facing sequence.
findings.verification: Source-observed editor behavior; exact public renderer was not compared in this scope.

findings.title: Website settings expose technical keys and untyped values
findings.observed: Setting labels are raw settingKey values; every value uses the same text input. Prefix splitting supplies the only grouping. Refresh overwrites edited rows. Public/private is editable per key.
findings.impact: Client staff must infer what a key means and can discard work or change public visibility without a readable change summary.
findings.recommendation: Add a metadata map for known keys with friendly labels/examples/typed controls, protect dirty refresh/navigation, and review visibility changes. Retain the rule that only backend-approved keys are edited.
findings.verification: Directly observed; the actual approved key list and response schema were not authenticated.

findings.title: Public scheduling asks Indian client staff to enter UTC manually
findings.observed: Blog publishing and announcement start/end inputs explicitly show UTC datetime-local fields.
findings.impact: Staff must mentally convert their intended publishing time; timezone mistakes are easier even though the label is technically explicit.
findings.recommendation: Accept and display the configured client/company timezone with a clear timezone label and preview sentence, convert to UTC for the existing API, and optionally show UTC in details.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed controls; no timezone conversion defect is claimed.

findings.title: Personal/browser preferences and business configuration look similar
findings.observed: Preferences and Settings both expose appearance. Manufacturing enabled state/default page size share a generic localStorage key; invoice template is also browser-local. The manufacturing setting label can be interpreted as enabling backend functionality.
findings.impact: A client may expect settings to apply to the company or follow their account on another machine, and may confuse manufacturing visibility with the missing company configuration discussed earlier.
findings.recommendation: Label these as This browser / My display preferences, group duplicate appearance entry points coherently, and keep company/backend setup in a separately labelled administrator area. Consider user/company scoped persistence only if required.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed local storage scope; broader deployment configuration was outside this subaudit.

findings.title: Several helpful summaries do not take the operator to the next task
findings.observed: HR dashboard pending approvals are noninteractive cards. Role creation and permission configuration are separate pages. Blog category maintenance exists in a tab but post category selection has no inline create option in the form.
findings.impact: Users re-find the same employee, role or category after switching menus.
findings.recommendation: Link HR cards to filtered lists; take new roles directly to their permission matrix; reuse category creation inline from the post editor. Use existing employee inline lookup flow as the model.
findings.verification: Source-observed navigation; proposed shortcuts are usability improvements, not missing core APIs.

findings.title: Technical implementation messages appear in ordinary client UI
findings.observed: Warranty summary says the backend has no CSV endpoint; self-profile fallback says the backend self-profile endpoint must be enabled; blog editor describes stored plain/Markdown format.
findings.impact: The client receives implementation details instead of a clear available action or understandable limitation.
findings.recommendation: Use action-oriented language such as Summary report available, Your account is view-only right now, or Write and preview your story. Keep API details in support disclosures/documentation.

findings.title: Payroll and leave side-panel queries need visible labels
findings.observed: Payroll employee/month/year query controls and Leave Balance/Pending Approvals selectors are rendered without explicit label props; surrounding headings do not identify each control individually.
findings.impact: The purpose of a selection/year field is harder to understand and screen-reader labelling is weaker.
findings.recommendation: Give each control a visible Employee, Payroll month, Payroll year or Approving manager label, maintain logical focus order and use named results below.
findings.verification: Directly observed parent props; full assistive-technology runtime audit was not performed.

findings.title: Payroll setup is a database foundation without an operator maintenance flow
findings.observed: SQL/domain defines salary structures, earning/deduction components, component amounts and effective employee assignments. No matching setup CRUD/assignment API in the inspected HR controllers, request types or IHrService, and no frontend form, were found. Payroll SQL creates a run then derives employees through CROSS APPLY/inner joins to configured salary structures/components; employees without setup do not enter its Salary result.
findings.impact: A normal operator cannot maintain the data that payroll depends on. A period can be processed while employees with missing salary setup are omitted; actual database setup has not been checked.
findings.recommendation: Define authorized salary-component/structure/effective-assignment setup APIs and UI. Before processing, show included staff, missing salary assignments/components, attendance completeness and period readiness, and block or explicitly resolve omissions. Review leave quota/paid-type setup similarly. Do not add frontend-only forms without backend support.
findings.verification: Source-confirmed schema and processing dependency; no database rows or live payroll runs were inspected.

findings.title: Department attendance report has no discovered operator surface
findings.observed: Backend department-report action and frontend service/Redux thunk exist. Unlike monthly reporting used by the employee modal, no page/component caller of the department-report action or thunk was found.
findings.impact: Available department-level attendance reporting is hard to reach from daily staff work.
findings.recommendation: Add a Department summary tab or link from attendance/HR dashboard with date/department filters and employee drill-down, reusing the existing endpoint.
findings.verification: Static endpoint/service/caller search; no hidden runtime plugin screens were tested.

strengths_to_preserve: Employee profile unifies overview, bank, documents, attendance and leaves; employee create supports saved drafts and inline creation of department/designation/shift.
Attendance has a real quick book with visible-staff bulk present/absent, per-employee exceptions and explicit Save/Reset.
Data Book already provides a substantial sheet workspace, Excel paste preview, keyboard cell navigation, row save/failure state, copy/history/privacy and row-version conflict handling.
Page administration already supports parent-child tree/table views, add child, icon preview and descendant-parent validation.
Permission matrix has search, bulk controls, dirty status and read-only effective SuperAdmin presentation.
Website product media validation, ordered benefits, sticky save, public-change confirmations and concurrency comparisons already exist.
Blog category maintenance is present in a nested tab, with automatic editable slugs and server conflict feedback.
Warranty separates internal notes and customer-visible messages, confirms customer sends, guards actions by state/permission and records history.
Activity log before/after comparison and advanced disclosure patterns are good examples to reuse instead of exposing raw technical data by default.
limitations: No live browser interactions, role logins, keyboard/screen-reader/mobile tests, network failure injection, database verification or authenticated end-to-end execution were performed in this subaudit.
Presence in source confirms implemented screens and intended service calls, not that every API works on the running database.

F:/FI/cosmos/frontend/src/services/website/websiteService.js:13 explicitly documents remaining authenticated response-shape verification for blog/categories, announcements, settings, warranty subresources and summary.

No dedicated frontend maintenance routes or owned HR controller/service setup commands were found for configurable holiday calendars, leave type quotas, salary components/structures/effective assignments or similar HR policies. Fixed enum options, embedded shift settings and salary/leave database/domain records do exist; foundation records are distinguished from an exposed maintenance API.
Recommendations involving company-level settings, new queues or new persistence must follow existing authorization and API contracts; this audit did not invent or mutate those contracts.
No claim of a fully tested or error-free project follows from this static review.
